author: user
text: Keep existing cursor signatures compatible. Add coverage for an empty final page and explain how to reproduce it.

author: assistant
text: The cursor encoder remains unchanged. I added an empty-page regression case and documented the reproduction using an exhausted cursor. I have not run the integration database here.

author: user
text: Why did we avoid putting a total row count into the cursor payload?

author: assistant
text: We kept the cursor opaque and stable because a changing total would invalidate old cursors. Page metadata can report counts separately without changing the pagination boundary.

author: user
text: Summarize the export audit work and what remains before we can close it.

author: assistant
text: The export filters and redaction checks are implemented. The staging export still needs a human check with a restricted account. My implementation claim does not establish that staging passed.

author: user
text: Make the sidebar usable with a keyboard and keep the active route visible at 200 percent zoom.

author: assistant
text: The sidebar now uses native buttons with a visible focus ring and a persistent active-route label. I checked the DOM structure; browser keyboard testing remains to be done.

author: user
text: Why do we keep sidebar groups expanded instead of remembering collapsed state?

author: assistant
text: For this release we kept groups expanded so all destinations remain discoverable. Persisting collapse state would add a hidden navigation state; we can revisit after observing usage.

author: user
text: What should I check when reviewing the color-token changes?

author: assistant
text: Review text contrast, focus outlines, and the disabled-button appearance in both themes. The screenshot comparison alone does not prove accessibility compliance.

author: user
text: Prevent two concurrent requests from refreshing the token at the same time.

author: assistant
text: The refresh path now shares one in-flight promise and retries each request once. I added a concurrent-request test; physical-device verification is still pending.

author: user
text: What should happen if the refresh request is rejected?

author: assistant
text: A rejected refresh clears the saved session and returns to sign-in. We avoid replaying the failed request indefinitely. The test covers a rejected promise, not a real identity-provider outage.

author: user
text: Where did we leave the device checks?

author: assistant
text: The simulator happy path is recorded. Offline-to-online recovery and expired refresh tokens still need a physical-device run. Keep those as unverified until there is an observed result.

author: user
text: Add idempotency to delivery retries without losing a valid second delivery.

author: assistant
text: The idempotency key uses the delivery identity plus destination. An explicit retry reuses that key; a distinct delivery has a distinct identity. A database uniqueness constraint remains the final guard.

author: user
text: Does the uniqueness constraint mean the race is fully resolved?

author: assistant
text: No. The constraint prevents duplicate persisted deliveries, but the external side effect can still happen before the second worker observes the conflict. We need a claim-before-send design and a concurrency run.

author: user
text: Summarize the unresolved worker-claim work.

author: assistant
text: The worker-claim change is drafted. It is blocked on deciding whether expired claims can be retried safely after an ambiguous provider response. No verified concurrency result is recorded.

author: user
text: Make sure branches cannot overwrite another branch cache entry.

author: assistant
text: The cache key now includes the lockfile hash and toolchain version. Fallback restoration is read-only for untrusted branches. These changes still need a complete hosted CI run.

author: user
text: Why allow a fallback cache if exact-key isolation matters?

author: assistant
text: The fallback restores reusable dependencies but never treats the result as a verification outcome. The job still installs from the lockfile and writes only to its exact trusted key.

author: user
text: What remains for staging access verification?

author: assistant
text: The access checklist is ready. An operator must sign in with the restricted account, attempt the protected route, and record the observed response. I have not performed that check.
